_comment: twist_lock_drill panel 0 'Twist-lock (backstep)'. Woman on a 20 deg overhang. Left arm LOCKED (elbow ~68 deg, elbow down at the ribs, hand by the left shoulder) on a big incut edge whose lip faces up-left (120 deg), thumb-up grip pulling down and in. Pelvis yaw 85 = right hip into the wall (pelvis surface touching it); chest yaw ~70 (twist -15) facing left, slight forward lean (bend 15) toward the locked hand; right shoulder ~3 cm off the wall. Right foot on a chip under the right hip, OUTSIDE edge, knee bent ~61 deg pointing left (body-front). Left foot on a lower-left chip, INSIDE edge, leg nearly straight (~162 deg). Right arm straight (~175 deg) up to a high jug. Head looks up toward the right hand (neck clamped at its limit). Camera: rear three-quarter from the climber's right at 30 deg (not 40: at 40 the locked forearm hides behind the torso), lens at hip height (elevation -3.5 with auto target). CAMFIX: identical pose; camera only changed to her open (left) side, front three-quarter, az -35, el 1 (lens slightly above hip height).
